question: T01: two bounded constants on one fixed regular spectral interval

comparison.allowed: Only alpha and beta, constant over the entire interval and over refinement.
physical_metrics: static full-line signed v mass normalized by 4L
static u maximum norm on a symmetric y strip
common-initial-data leading u error velocity over the full x,y plane
comparison.boundary_for_physical_proofs: Full x and y line with decay and compatible zero far field; finite boundaries require additional terms.

predictions.statement: Leading phase minimax residual is C_Gamma Delta_A^2/8, attained uniquely at alpha=-2 C_Gamma m, beta=C_Gamma(m^2-d^2/2), if this pair is feasible.

For the normalized phase coefficient, tenfold improvement requires spectral scale ratio R=max|A|/min|A| <= 5+2sqrt(5). Strict inequality and feasibility permit sufficiently small h, with explicit remainder margin. Equality requires separate finite-h analysis.
At any nonzero h, exact matching of the longitudinal phase on a nontrivial open spectral interval is impossible because chi is rational and exp(h L(A)) is not.

For the same-spectrum finite-h N=1 Gram solution, integral_x v_h=4 log(chi)/h. Its normalized mass defect is exactly the phase defect; the full-line L1 physical v error is at least its absolute value times 4|L|.

With common physical initial data and decaying full-line boundary, integral_x(v_h-v_0)=0 for all times for which the solutions exist. The static phase-mass witness therefore cancels exactly after initial correction.

Conditional common-initial-data leading u error velocity equals F_Gamma(z)/A+alpha G_Gamma(z)/A^2; beta does not enter. Endpoint elimination yields optimized-to-original velocity ratio at least r(1-r)/(1+r^2), r=min|A|/max|A|. At R=2 this is 1/5, despite phase allowing 1/32.

directed_checks.purpose: Exact symbolic identities and a few predeclared finite-h evaluations; never fit parameters from PDE output.
directed_checks.check_points: Only interval endpoints and midpoint, to check alternating leading values and remainder; no parameter scan.

limitations: Phase factor is not the ratio of full u/v errors.
Static exact-family comparisons use different initial physical fields.
Common-initial-data finite positive time conclusions need a uniform evolution/Taylor remainder in a specified admissible function space.
No claim of external literature originality.
